content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: the loan-campaign surge is being absorbed, with 93.9% service level predicted for 14:45-18:45 against an 80% target.","why":"Accounts & General is running 44% over forecast (2,409 calls vs 1,669), driven by loan and offer enquiries from the MKT-2026-551 pre-approved loan email. Staffing is above plan and handle time is normal, so current staffing is already absorbing the extra demand. With no changes, service level is predicted at 93.9% over the disruption window (payments 95.7%, general 92.0%), with 1.1% abandons and 89.6% for the rest of the day. This meets the target at zero cost and with no policy issues.","trade_offs":["P1 (callbacks and break smoothing) is also free and policy-compliant but predicts slightly lower at 93.7% (rest of day 88.7%), so it adds work for no gain.","P2 (loan self-service) would raise the window to 95.3% and cut abandons to 0.6% for 36 INR, but it breaks CX-01: a known-issue message needs a confirmed outage or incident, and this is a campaign, not an outage.","P3 (combined demand reduction) gives the best results, at 95.8% for the window, 93.8% for the rest of the day and 0.5% abandons. However, it costs 528 INR, also breaks CX-01, and deflects payments customers who are not affected."],"watch":"Keep an eye on general queue volume, especially loan_enquiry and new_offer_enquiry, in case campaign calls rise further toward evening. If general drops toward 80%, consider the no-cost P1 actions. Also consider asking marketing whether a compliant self-service route for loan activation can be set up."}
